notes:
- RESULT: no validated way found to start a non-holyagent agent or to reach Function or a host global by name. Every earlier finding is closed, with reasons below. Two open items are non-blocking suspicions, because their impact depends on the Workflow sandbox, which is not in the repo and which I could not inspect.
- CLOSED eof0 #1 (whitespace lookalike fused into an identifier): acorn treats NBSP, U+FEFF and similar as real whitespace, so `agent<NBSP>(...)` parses as a real agent() call and goes through agentCall (workflow-check.ts:399-438). Non-ASCII identifier characters that are not ID_Start/ID_Continue are parse errors, which means a refusal.
- CLOSED eof0 #2 (`5..constructor`): acorn produces a MemberExpression with property `constructor`, which memberExpression refuses through DENIED_NAMES (workflow-check.ts:393). Hex, `1_0` and `10n` are handled by acorn, and bigint is refused at :475.
- CLOSED eof0 #3, gcrq, kuyn and yhba (string, template, concatenated or quoted constructor keys, `Array.of['constructor']`, `of` before `[`): the only computed access allowed is a non-negative integer literal (memberExpression :386-391). Computed keys are refused in objects (objectProperty :372), in patterns (declarePattern :318-326, where a quoted key gives nameOf undefined) and in agent options (:418). `of` and `yield` have no special status any more.
- CLOSED gcrq and kuyn Bun/fetch/setTimeout: a free name is allowed only if it is in GLOBALS or bound (:648-653). declare() refuses any declaration of a GLOBALS, HOST_GLOBALS or DENIED_NAMES name, or of `agent` (:283-287). All binders go through declare: declarePattern, FunctionExpression names, FunctionDeclaration, catch, and var/let/const. The only other scope write is `meta`. So parameter, catch, block-const and function-name shadowing of fetch, Bun or process are refused, and a shadowed `agent` is impossible. Because bound() is resolved at the end over real scopes, var hoisting and function hoisting cannot make a global look declared.
- CLOSED yhba/gcrq optional items: agent() option keys are limited to AGENT_OPTIONS (:418-425), a spread or computed key is refused, there is exactly one agentType, and its value must be a Literal string (acorn-cooked, so `worker` equals what the engine reads) in the 18-entry SPECIALISTS set (:428-433). Depth is capped at MAX_DEPTH 120, and parser or walk stack overflow is caught by Effect.try and becomes a refusal (:664-668).
- OPEN, non-blocking, suspicion (S1): builtins and runtime objects can be mutated, which contradicts the doc line 'It may not assign to a global or into one (`Math.max = …`)'. writeTarget (:458-466) checks only that the root name is bound, so `const M = Math; M.max = () => 1` and `const b = budget; b.x = 1` pass. A direct `Object.assign(Math, { max: () => 1 })` or `Object.assign(JSON, { stringify: fn })` also passes: `assign` is in CALLABLE_PROPERTIES, `Math` and `JSON` are free GLOBALS, and no assignment node appears. DENIED_NAMES is a syntactic check, so a dynamic string reaches a denied key: `Object.assign(Error, Object.fromEntries([['prepareStackTrace', (e, sites) => sites]]))` followed by `Error('x').stack` passes (key is a string literal; assign, fromEntries and Error() are all allowed). Prototypes are unreachable, since `prototype`, `__proto__` and `getPrototypeOf` are denied and there are no dynamic reads, so I found no path to Object.prototype pollution. Impact exists only if the Workflow runtime evaluates scripts in the same realm as host code that later calls the patched builtin (a callback that receives host arguments such as agent options) or reads `.stack` of a host error. I could not confirm that. Add one script of this shape to the refusal tests, and either refuse `Object.assign`, `Object.fromEntries`, `freeze` and the like when the first argument is not a script-created literal, or confirm that the sandbox is a separate realm.
- OPEN, non-blocking, suspicion (S2): the CALLABLE_PROPERTIES list and the `call/apply/bind` denial are only syntactic. `[x].map(obj.method, obj)` passes a thisArg (map, forEach, filter, find, some, every and flatMap are all listed), so any method read by name can be called with a chosen `this`, and `const g = obj.method; g()` calls it without one. I found no builtin reachable under these rules that runs code (no Function, no global object, no Symbol, no Reflect). This is defense in depth only. I would not rely on the list as a barrier against future allowlist additions.
- Note: `budget` is exempt from CALLABLE_PROPERTIES (:395), so any method chain on it is free (`budget.x.y.z()`), and `Object.assign(budget, …)` is allowed. If the budget object has a setter or an extender, a script could raise its own limit. The budget API is not documented in the repo, so this is unvalidated.
- Note: parser versus engine. The script is parsed as a module (strict). If the runtime instead evaluates a sloppy script or an AsyncFunction wrapper after stripping the `export`, then HTML-style comments (`<!--`, `-->`) in the engine can only hide text acorn has already checked as code, and `this` is refused, so there is no divergence that hides code from the checker. If the runtime pre-processes the `export const meta` line with a regex, I could not check what that does to string content. Unvalidated.
- Checked and found sound: all expression and statement types outside the closed set (new, tagged templates, classes, labels, sequences, delete, yield, import, with, regex, private names) fall to the default refusal. Optional calls and calls of call results are refused. `agent` as a value, alias, argument, member-call or shorthand is refused as an unbound name. A bare `agent(...)` needs two arguments with an object literal second. `export` forms other than a single `export const meta` of pure literals are refused. Declared names in nested function and arrow parameters and defaults are walked. Every sub-expression of a call, member, template, array, object, conditional, for-in/of, try and switch is visited, so I found no unwalked child where code could hide. INLINE_INPUTS keeps scriptPath, name and resumeFromRunId on the normal flow (hook.ts change).
- Dependency: acorn is pinned at 8.19.0 in packages/runtime/package.json and bun.lock:145 with an sha512 integrity hash. It was already in the lockfile as a transitive dependency of espree. It is a parser and runs nothing, so there is no concern.
- Tests: the added tests cover the earlier bypasses but none of the S1 or S2 shapes. Over-refusal that fails closed (index by a variable, depth over 120, a declared name such as `call` or `bind`, Date) is not a security finding.
